newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wins over anti-abortion protester.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wins over anti-abortion protester.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday won over a young woman who tearfully protested his veto of a ban on certain late-term abortions after he paused along a campaign ropeline to explain his position to her.

The protester -- Mary Ellen Savoie of Sulphur, Louisiana -- intercepted Clinton while he was shaking hands after a rally at the Northrop-Grumman plant in Lake Charles. Savoie, a teenager who described herself as "very pro-life," was in tears during her five-minute chat with the president.
"He explained to me why he vetoed that measure," she told reporters later, referring to Clinton's controversial refusal to sign a proposed ban on so-called partial birth abortions.

Clinton has said he vetoed the bill because the Republican-led Congress refused to make exceptions from the ban in cases where the life of the mother was threatened or severe health consequences could result from carrying the pregnancy to term.

Savoie, who apparently was not old enough to vote, said she "felt better" about Clinton's position after hearing from him personally and felt she could could now "tell my mother it's all right to vote for him."

Observers have long marvelled at the way Clinton is able to connect with the crowds who attend his rallies, but Savoie's case was the first documented incident of him making an actual political conversion.
